title: Your Credit Card Has DLC (And You’re Paying for It)
title_alternatives: The $200 Credit Card That Lost to a Free One
Your Credit Card Rewards Have a Spending Problem
description:
Dave buys a fictional premium credit card and discovers four expensive traps: inflated point totals, interest, bonus chasing, and deferred-interest fine print. Original stick-figure finance comedy. All card offers and rewards calculations in this story are illustrative; actual terms vary. No sponsored offer or affiliate recommendation is included.

Example math: 30,000 points × $0.007 = $210; $210 + $60 useful credits − $200 fee = $70; $200 cash back − $70 = $130 difference. Simplified interest: $1,000 × 24% × 30/365 ≈ $19.73. A $1,200 balance divided over 12 months is $100/month before any applicable fees or other charges.

The $19.73 estimate assumes a constant $1,000 balance already subject to interest, no applicable grace period, a 365-day year, and simple interest without compounding. Actual issuer calculations can differ. The $100/month illustration assumes all twelve payments reach the promotional principal, no added charges, and payoff before the actual promotional deadline.

Sources (CFPB):
https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/what-is-a-daily-periodic-rate-on-a-credit-card-en-46/
https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/how-does-my-credit-card-company-calculate-the-amount-of-interest-i-owe-en-51/
https://www.consumerfinance.gov/archive/blog/how-understand-special-promotional-financing-offers-credit-cards/
https://www.consumerfinance.gov/ask-cfpb/i-got-a-credit-card-promising-no-interest-for-a-purchase-if-i-pay-in-full-within-12-months-how-does-this-work-en-40/

chapters.source_narration: Rule one. If the reward changes what Dave buys, it may not be a reward anymore.

chapters.title: The monthly-credit trap
chapters.source_narration: But wait. My premium card has monthly credits. Ten dollars. Every month. Free money, right?

chapters.title: Settle the annual score
chapters.source_narration: Now settle the year. Premium rewards: two hundred ten. Useful credits: sixty. Fee: minus two hundred.

chapters.source_narration: Dave demands a rematch. Points Monk agrees, but looking expensive earns no points this time. The contestants must survive on what they actually do for Dave.

chapters.source_narration: Imagine twelve hundred dollars with twelve months available. Simple planning target: one hundred dollars a month.
